comparator.name: Medicine (Geneeskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 Medicine EER applies to the first entering cohort of the new De Nieuwe Utrechtse Arts curriculum and establishes a 180-EC bachelor comprising a 165-EC compulsory Medicine major and 15 EC of genuine profile space. Appendix 1b gives the complete DNUA major. The four 3-EC carousel courses are all compulsory: three are taken in Year 1 and one in Year 2, with order depending on group allocation. The EER is used for exact credits where the current student overview remains provisional: Bewegen & Waarnemen and Levensloop are each 10 EC in the adopted EER, not the earlier 9.5-EC webpage figures. The 15-EC profile space is preserved generically rather than filled with invented electives. All 180 EC are thereby accounted for. Fixed-queue review on 2026-10-16 verified the current adopted EER Appendix 1b and DNUA overview. All settled components, credits and cohort-specific route are preserved. The EER still gives 10 EC each for Bewegen & Waarnemen and Levensloop, overriding the webpage’s 9.5-EC entries.

routeSelection.basis: DNUA is the formally adopted curriculum for all students entering Medicine in 2026–27; the predecessor CRU+ curriculum accepted its final entrants in 2025–26. DNUA is therefore the only cohort-applicable curriculum for this Fall-2026 comparison and is selected independently of UCR fit.

core: Human biology, organ-system physiology, anatomy, disease mechanisms and pharmacology
Clinical reasoning, diagnosis, treatment and supervised patient care
Medical science, research methods and evidence evaluation
Relationship between physical health, mental health and nervous-system function
Disease prevention, management and population health
Ethical reasoning and the social context of health and care
adjacent: Biopsychosocial health, mental illness and cognitive function
questions: How do biological mechanisms produce illness and treatment effects?
How do brain function, behaviour and social circumstances connect physical and mental health?

candidates.label: Physical and mental health through psychology and cognitive science

alternatives.label: Biomedical disease mechanisms, health & research
alternatives.labelReason: Twenty health, cognition and life-science courses dominate the completed curriculum, supported by research methods, data analysis and ethics plus PPD. The title describes biomedical and psychological study of health and disease, without implying Medicine or clinical competence.
alternatives.concept: Study human health and disease through cellular biology, anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, genetics, immunity, pharmacology, laboratory methods, epidemiology and psychological influences on illness. Research design, statistics, data handling and evidence synthesis support scientific investigation. This is a biomedical and health-science response to Medicine; supervised clinical reasoning, practical medical skills and patient care remain absent.
progression: Biomedical and brain/behaviour gateways precede all dependent courses. Cell biology, physiology, biochemistry and anatomy precede advanced pathology and pharmacology where feasible. Research Methods & Statistics precedes experimental statistics and the meta-analysis seminar. Formal prerequisites and exact planned availability pass. Data handling occurs before final-year evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: Physical and mental health: psychology, cognition & behaviour
alternatives.labelReason: Seventeen health, psychology, cognition and biomedical courses form the core, supported by sociology, qualitative inquiry, statistics, data analysis, ethical reasoning and persuasive communication plus PPD. Cognitive and language-function courses are bounded contributors to understanding impairment; the programme does not imply clinical training.
alternatives.concept: Investigate connections between physical and mental health through physiology, neurobiology, cognitive function, psychopathology, health psychology and lifespan development. Combine this with epidemiology, pharmacology, social influences, qualitative inquiry and quantitative evidence to study illness experience, psychological interventions and health behaviour. Persuasion contributes methods for analysing health messages; language neuroscience contributes the study of language impairment. These are academic perspectives rather than medical consultation or supervised treatment.
alternatives.distinctness: Six courses / 45 EC differ in each direction. Molecular cell biology, biochemistry, molecular pathology, infection/immunity, mechanisms of disease and laboratory work give way to perception/action, language neuroscience, social psychology, sociology, qualitative inquiry and persuasive communication. The organising priority changes from molecular/organ-system disease investigation to cognitive, psychological and social connections between physical and mental health.
progression: Brain/behaviour and biomedical gateways precede dependent cognition, psychology and pharmacology. Social psychology precedes advanced health psychology; sociology precedes qualitative inquiry. Introductory research methods precede experimental statistics and evidence synthesis. Neurobiology precedes Higher Order Functions and advanced language neuroscience. All exact terms and formal prerequisites pass; persuasive communication follows social psychology and ethics, but prior rhetoric is advisory rather than a formal prerequisite.

selection.assessment: Two complete programmes are included in sequence. Prevention and disease management (14925) are already substantively represented through epidemiology, disease mechanisms, immunity, pharmacology and health psychology in the closest response and through health behaviour and psychological intervention in the second. Scientific and ethical practice (14926) is implemented through research methods, evidence synthesis and ethical reasoning. No remaining generator-eligible row supplies a further distinct academic priority: clinical diagnosis/treatment and symptoms (14920/14923) remain explicit gaps, not a licence to substitute a computing or generic leadership programme. A third reorganisation of these same evidenced concerns is not included merely by swapping courses. Public health, imaging and doctor-patient communication are support-only curricular topics; alone they do not generate additional routes.

blocks: Biomedical foundations, organ systems & treatment mechanisms

Both supply foundations in health, biological function and disease. The medical component integrates its own curriculum-specific knowledge; UCR is a cellular/molecular gateway, not equal medical coverage.
Human Physiology includes cardiovascular and respiratory function. This is a partial scientific correspondence, not the integrated clinical teaching in the external course.
Both concern metabolism. UCR covers molecular biochemistry rather than the full digestive-system medical component.
Both explicitly teach pharmacology. UCR teaches drug mechanisms and quantitative pharmacology; it does not supply supervised clinical prescribing or pharmacotherapeutic competence.

This distinct medical component retains its own scope and credits. Related anatomy, physiology, genetics and disease courses do not reproduce the integrated medical component and are not counted again.

notes.text: Utrecht’s Medicine curriculum integrates biomedical and organ-system study with clinical reasoning, practical skills, community and workplace experience, professional assessment and a medical thesis. These UCR programmes study biomedical disease mechanisms and the connections between physical and mental health. They do not provide the medical clinical sequence or supervised patient care.
